answer: A coastal market stays honest when standing is earned through distinct deliveries. The first newcomer completes 1 delivery for a different merchant, the tenth completes 10, and the twentieth completes 20, each checked by its own merchant and never reused. An operator spinning up fakes faces a cost that climbs with every name: 20 fakes demand 210 deliveries, and one timber load counts for only one identity, however many names ride along. Like a pearl growing one layer at a time, seen truly only through a prism, every extra identity adds another full round of real work.
